spotlight.label: Spotlight
spotlight.title: COP31 in Antalya
spotlight.intro: Bangladesh wants adaptation finance tripled and paid as grants, not loans, plus real money for loss and damage. Devlens follows what the summit means for the sector until the talks close.

today.text: The COP31 Presidency has published the first draft of the summit's main political decision. The 18-page text calls for tripling adaptation finance for developing countries to at least $120 billion a year by 2035, and asks developed countries to set out a roadmap to get there. It also proposes an Antalya-to-Addis Ababa Roadmap to find new and predictable money for adaptation and loss and damage, with a report due at COP32. Chris Bowen, who chairs the talks, said not all parties will agree with every element and the text will be cut down before Friday. Separately, at a D-8 ministerial session, Bangladesh called for grant-based and highly concessional climate finance, technology sharing and closer cooperation.

watch: Adaptation finance: the first draft names a figure, at least $120 billion a year by 2035. Watch whether it survives into the final text, which nearly 200 countries must approve by Friday.
Just transition: the draft calls for a "just, orderly and equitable" move away from fossil fuels. Whether the Belém-Antalya Action Mechanism is adopted is still to be decided.
Finance on the agenda: tripling is now in the draft text, but it is not agreed. African countries have warned that the draft risks distracting from accountability on climate finance.
Gender: UN Women found 73% of countries recognise gender-specific climate risks, but just over one in three address them fully.
